measured_on.guest: macOS 27.2 (26B123) arm64, tart clone of ntfsmac-golden
measured_on.mount_as: normal user, image file (not a block device)

classes.effective: accepted and the effect was observed
classes.ignored: accepted (exit 0, mount appears) with no observable effect
classes.rejected: ntfs-3g or libfuse refuses it: non-zero exit status and a message
classes.silent: accepted but the stated behaviour is not delivered; the daemon must check the precondition itself
classes.by-source: accepted; the effect is known from the NTFS-3G source but was not observed in the matrix

always.note: without it (or with any other value) ntfs-3g exits 0, no mount appears, SIGTERM is ignored; SIGKILL needed
mount source becomes /dev/diskNsM and the mount gets the local flag; without it the source is macfuse://UUID
consumed by the engine (ctx->recover = FALSE); acts only on an unclean $LogFile, not exercised here (needs the unclean-log fixture)

checked on disk with ntfsinfo: atime unchanged after a read; with atime/relatime it is updated. Not visible in stat through the backend. Kept (T-M3-06, I-META-03): with atime, relatime or no option a read moves atime on disk, and the stat view stays stale until a remount

creating a:b, CON, aux.txt, trail., 'sp ', q?x, a"b, lt<x, a*b, pipe|x fails with EINVAL; without it all succeed. Also applies to xattr (named-stream) names until patch 0009 (ADR-025): com.apple.metadata:_kMDItemUserTags (Finder tags) and other names with : give EINVAL (T-M3-08, I-XATTR-05)

ADR-012 compression row (owner decision 2026-11-15, T-M3-24): new files in a compressed directory are stored plain (without it NTFS-3G compresses them); existing compressed files are still read and updated (T-M3-09, docs/spikes/M3-readpath-big.md). Confirmed on macOS by I-BIG-COMP-01

keeps ntfs-3g in the foreground: without it the engine calls daemon() after the mount request, so the spawned process exits 0 at once and the real worker runs in a new session and process group. The daemon must supervise the real worker (exit status, unmount before exit, SIGKILL of its process group; ARCHITECTURE sections 4.1 and 7), so it is mandatory (M3 audit F-01). Used by every supervised integration case since T-M2-03 (docs/spikes/M2-backend.md)

all xattr names work (com.apple.*, com.test.x, user.*) and survive a remount; xattr only keeps user.* and fails the rest with ENOTSUP. Kept after T-M3-08: names at most 127 bytes, values at most 262143 bytes; com.apple.FinderInfo must be 32 bytes and an all-zero value reads as ENOATTR; windows_names refuses names with : until patch 0009
accepted; ownership shown by the mount is the mounting user regardless (noowners); decimal required
files show -rw-r--r--. Display only: the execute bit is not checked (a 0644 binary runs, I-PERM-05) and nothing on disk depends on it; kept as a display value (ADR-012, 2026-11-15)

opt_in.note: engine opens the volume read-only (Mounted ... Read-Only), mount shows read-only, image bytes unchanged

files with the DOS hidden attribute leave the listing; stat by name still works. hide_dot_files (writes HIDDEN on new dot-names) and show_sys_files (lists the NTFS system files) stay out of the allow-list (T-M3-06, I-META-07)

opt_in.requires: the file must exist: a missing file is accepted silently (class silent) and the mount behaves as without it
opt_in.note: turns on NTFS permissions; chmod works and persists across remounts, also together with uid/gid. Modes are stored and shown, not enforced (I-PERM-07). A mapping file whose implicit line (::SID) ends in a number below 1000 is accepted with the message Bad implicit SID pattern and the line is dropped (I-PERM-06); the daemon's file check should also refuse such a line

opt_in.requires: do not combine with uid, gid, fmask or dmask: with them chmod returns success but the mode does not change
opt_in.note: works alone (chmod 600 shown as -rw-------, persists). Observed in T-M3-20: files made before permissions was turned on show 0777; modes 0600, 0700 and 000 are stored and shown but not enforced (another local account reads and writes them, I-PERM-07)
